paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The LORD sees pride, and He doesn't let it stand. The daughters of Zion were haughty, walking with "heads held high," and the LORD said their finery would be taken away (Isaiah 3:16, 18). I bet that's because anything we lean on to make ourselves look big can't hold us up when it counts.

But hear this, because it matters. The passage doesn't end in sackcloth. Isaiah says "the Branch of the LORD will be beautiful and glorious," and that whoever remains will be called holy (Isaiah 4:2-3). The Lord washes away the filth and cleanses the bloodstains, and the baker doesn't have to scrub that off alone (Isaiah 4:4).

And look where it lands: a canopy, "a shelter to give shade from the heat by day, and a refuge and hiding place from the storm and the rain" (Isaiah 4:6). I spent years in a drawer holding onto whatever shine I had left, and let me tell you, the shelter was never my doing. So baker, put down the jingling stuff and run to the LORD's covering. That story isn't over, and it ends with Him as your refuge.
